items.stem: According to Newton's first law, what happens to an object moving at constant velocity when the net external force is zero?

options.text: It will eventually come to rest.
It continues moving at the same speed and direction.

items.explanation: With zero net force, the object continues at the same speed and direction; a force is not required to keep it moving.

items.stem: A hockey puck slides on a perfectly frictionless ice surface. No external forces act on it after the initial push. What will happen to its motion?

options.text: It will gradually slow down because a force is needed to keep it moving.
It will accelerate because its inertia pushes it forward.
It will stop due to air resistance.
It will slide at a constant speed in a straight line.

items.explanation: With no net force, the puck maintains its velocity; it neither slows down nor speeds up.

items.stem: A deep‑space probe drifts far from any planet with its engines turned off, experiencing essentially zero net external force. How will its velocity change over time?

options.text: Its speed will slowly decrease because a force is required to maintain motion.
Its speed will increase as a result of its inertia.
Its velocity will oscillate due to unseen cosmic forces.

items.explanation: In the absence of net force, the probe’s velocity remains unchanged; it coasts indefinitely at the same speed and direction.
